findings.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.3.2, 19.2.6, 19.1.8
findings.summary_md: GitLab's September 10, 2026 critical patch release shipped 19.3.2, 19.2.6, and 19.1.8, fixing 18 issues including CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N, reported by s3ntago via HackerOne) and CVE-2026-87719 (CVSS 9.9 EE GraphQL subscription serializer deserialization, reported by kyyblin). The advisory lists wider affected ranges than most coverage repeated: CE/EE all versions from 18.7 before 18.11.12 and 19.0 before 19.0.9, in addition to 19.1 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2. It also credits the same release with CVE-2026-88765, a CVSS 8.5 authenticated RCE in the Advanced Search Unicode conversion wrapper, and links three GitLab threat detections for CVE-2026-85706 exploitation attempts.

findings.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.2.4, 19.1.6, 19.0.8, 18.11.11
findings.summary_md: GitLab's August 17, 2026 critical patch release fixed CVE-2026-19478, a CVSS 9.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:H) issue allowing an unauthenticated user to remotely modify or delete public projects and user data via a GraphQL directive, affecting CE/EE from 18.2 before 18.11.11, 19.0 before 19.0.8, 19.1 before 19.1.6, and 19.2 before 19.2.4, reported by hiimguardian through HackerOne. This is the earlier critical GitLab flaw watchTowr cited as almost immediately exploited in the wild, the precedent that frames the September release as the second max-severity GitLab emergency in a month.

findings.title: GitLab Critical Security Release: 16.0.1
findings.summary_md: GitLab's May 23, 2023 critical security release fixed CVE-2023-2825, a CVSS 10.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N) unauthenticated arbitrary file read via uploads path traversal, affecting only version 16.0.0 and exploitable when an attachment existed in a public project nested within at least five groups; reported by pwnie via HackerOne. This is the direct precedent for the September 2026 commits API flaw in the story record's CVE list, and the contrast in preconditions is stark: five nested groups then, any single public project now.
